mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has risen monotonically from +6.3% to +14.7% over four weeks, indicating sustained indoor confinement. This persistent lockdown state suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility through behavioral avoidance, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds mean over last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL mobility declines for two consecutive weeks before the end of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has collapsed from +21.6% to -5.3% over four weeks, signaling a shift from panic-buying to essential-only trips. This behavioral reorientation toward necessity reduces discretionary retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to remain depressed or decline further over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined 27.2 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains negative.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has fallen sharply to -31.9%, indicating near-total collapse of public transportation use. This transit collapse removes a key access pathway to retail districts, mechanically reducing RETAIL_REC footfall over the next four weeks independent of demand.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -31.9% in t-0w, lowest of all categories
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while TRANSIT remains below -25 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined to -32.4%, indicating widespread remote work adoption. Concurrent RESIDENTIAL elevation to +14.7% reflects home-based activity concentration. This dual shift reduces commute-linked retail exposure and substitutes home-based consumption for in-person retail, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and RESIDENTIAL moved in opposite directions across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days exceeds baseline by more than 5 percentage points, or WORKPLACES recovers above -20 percentage points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has fallen to -41.6%, the lowest of all categories, indicating severe outdoor activity suppression consistent with winter weather and/or lockdown enforcement. This outdoor suppression will persist into the next four weeks, keeping populations indoors and away from retail-adjacent outdoor spaces, maintaining RETAIL_REC depression.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -41.6% in t-0w, tied with RETAIL_REC as lowest
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -20 percentage points within two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not follow within one week.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized collapse across RETAIL_REC (-41.0%), PARKS (-41.6%), TRANSIT (-31.9%), and WORKPLACES (-32.4%) in t-0w indicates a discrete policy shock (e.g., lockdown announcement or variant surge response). This shock will persist through the next two weeks before behavioral adaptation or policy reversal occurs, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
candidate_trigger: four or more mobility categories simultaneously fall below -30 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:All four categories reached lowest values in t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 10 percentage points within two weeks of the decision date, or any of the four proxies recovers above -20 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined monotonically from -11.1% to -41.0% over four weeks, establishing a clear downward trend. Absent a reversal signal in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES, this trend will continue over the next four weeks, with RETAIL_REC remaining below current levels due to momentum and path-dependent behavioral adjustment.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined 29.9 percentage points over four weeks with no reversal
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is higher than mean over last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has crossed from positive (+21.6%) to negative (-5.3%), while RETAIL_REC has fallen to -41.0%. This divergence indicates consumers are prioritizing essential purchases and avoiding discretionary retail. If GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes above -10% over the next two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -35%, it signals a bifurcation of consumer behavior that will sustain retail suppression.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC diverged sharply in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -10 percentage points.
